To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the B vitamins folic acid, B-6, and B-12 are effective in enhancing treatment response to antidepressant medications for depression; 2) the B vitamins are safe and well tolerated; 3) there are no differences in the efficacy of the B vitamins between middle-aged and older individuals; and 4) there are no significant differences in the efficacy between individuals who have mild, moderate, or severe depression.

the addition of a B vitamin supplement containing 400 μg of folate, 100 μg of vitamin B12, 20 mg of vitamin B6, and 10 mg of vitamin B2 to antidepressant therapy was not effective in improving the treatment response in patients with major depression, regardless of age.

the combination of vitamin B12, vitamin B6 and folic acid supplementation with antidepressants is more effective than placebo in improving treatment response in middle-aged and elderly adults with MDD, and that the effect is most pronounced in patients with low folate status.
